items.headline: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city
items.blurb: One evacuated couple says they crossed minefields in Oleshky in search of food.
items.text: Olha has one word to describe what life has been like in the front-line city of Oleshky over the past few years: "Horror". Disembarking alongside her from a coach in the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv with their immediate family and dog, her husband Viacheslav put it this way: "We came back from hell." The couple were among hundreds of residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city who crossed into northern Ukraine via Belarus on Saturday, many reuniting with loved ones they had not seen for years. Oleshky, seized by Russia during the first few days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River and on the other side by Russian forces. Olha and Viacheslav had lived there with their son and daughter, both in their 30s. Even as the shelling around them intensified, they feared that trying to escape could be even more dangerous, with routes mined and subject to drone attack. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area. items.headline: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
items.blurb: Oleshky residents had been without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.
items.text: There were raw emotional scenes as people evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky crossed from Belarus into the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv. Families cried as they reunited with relatives they had not seen for years, with two sisters running and crying out as they embraced their father. Some elderly residents were so weak they were carried on stretchers. They had been trapped in the frontline city without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked US First Lady Melania Trump for her efforts in brokering a local ceasefire that paved the way for their evacuation on Friday. Upon their arrival, Dasha and Anya Palii sprinted across the tarmac screaming towards the bus carrying their father Mykhailo. Their cries and their tears captured the sheer relief of three years of desperate worry, fearing they would never see him again. items.headline: Polish president holds crisis talks in court standoff
items.blurb: A dispute over the politicisation of Poland's constitutional court is deepening, with no side appearing to back down.
items.text: The Polish president has held crisis talks with political leaders as a dispute over the independence of the country’s top constitutional court deepens. Representatives of nationalist, far-right, and some governing coalition parties attended President Karol Nawrocki’s talks at the presidential palace on Saturday, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s governing centrist party, Civic Coalition, stayed away. Nawrocki said in a statement that he convened the “urgent” consultations “due to the threat to Poland’s internal security” presented by the sudden suspension on Friday of the Constitutional Tribunal’s chief judge, Bogdan Swieczkowski. Meanwhile, in a Saturday evening speech addressing the ongoing crisis, Tusk accused conservative nationalist opposition leaders of wanting to “destroy democracy and rule of law”. “Let’s call things by their name,” he said. “For years in Poland there exist organisations and politicians who wish to destroy democracy and rule of law.” Followers of the opposition right-wing Law and Justice party (PiS) gathered outside the court on Saturday, extending protests that have been running for weeks in support of PiS-friendly judges. The Constitutional Tribunal is Poland’s top court for deciding constitutional matters.

The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked. Rights groups and others have for years documented evidence of UAE support for the RSF, which has been accused of atrocities during the course of its war against the Sudanese army, including an attack on the city of El Fasher in October 2025 that the UN said had “hallmarks of genocide” . Nusseibeh, the UAE’s representative to the UN until 2024, has repeatedly reflected the UAE’s blanket denials of the accusations. items.headline: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
items.blurb: More than 320,000 people demonstrated across France against the rising cost of living and poor public services, with clashes between some protesters and police.
items.text: Hundreds of thousands of protesters demonstrated across France as the country prepares for a general strike in the coming days. In Paris, police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in a third weekend of nationwide demonstrations against the rising cost of living and poor public services. More than 320,000 people took to the streets around the country and at least 290 protesters were arrested, according to France's interior ministry. Police say about 70,000 demonstrated in Paris. The authorities prepared extensively to avoid a repeat of the violence, rioting and looting that happened two weeks ago. Protests also took place in Albania, Germany and Italy as youth take to the streets across Europe, the BBC's correspondent James Waterhouse reports.

items.text: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country. Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt. According to Mada Masr, Attalah was released after the news outlet had paid a fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100), prompting statements of support from global human rights groups. “Lina Attalah was released after we paid the said fine,” said her lawyer Hassan al-Azhari. “In the process, we discovered that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to a year in prison, as well as a fine of 20,000 Egyptian pounds,” he told AFP. items.headline: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
items.blurb: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) says North Korea was responsible for the hack.
items.text: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday. The remaining 10% may take longer to source in the required amounts, the company added. Binance has consistently pledged to cover 100% of the losses from what is suspected to be crypto's biggest hack on record and said it has set aside more than $6.34bn in company funds to do so. "Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the hack. Two analytics firms previously told the BBC they had robust intelligence pointing to North Korean state-backed hacking unit the Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor - which was specifically named by the FBI - as the likely culprits. Binance said it had replenished the stolen assets using various funds and its own corporate treasury. items.text: Three people belonging to the Kuki community were killed in a gunfight between rival armed groups in Manipur's Noney district, police said. The gunfight broke out at Kekru Naga village on Saturday (October 31) morning. The exchange of fire continued for several hours in the forested hill village, leaving three people dead, they said. Meanwhile, the Kuki Inpi Manipur (KIM), the apex body of the Kuki community, strongly condemned the killing of the three youths. In a statement, KIM alleged that "Naga militant groups" were behind the killings and demanded "justice, accountability and immediate state action". items.headline: Unpacking the brawl that sparked the Naga-Kuki conflict in Manipur
items.blurb: Personnel from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and the Border Security Force (BSF) were tasked with keeping the two communities apart.
items.text: A pitch-dark road, a flash of torchlight, flaring tempers and a drunken brawl. On February 7 this year, a Manipur village that was until then spared from the ethnic violence that had engulfed much of the state became the site of an altercation that opened a new front of conflict. What appeared to be a minor street tussle in a region besieged by brutality and bloodshed went on to expose decades-old Naga-Kuki fault lines, which were overshadowed at the time by the Meitei-Kuki conflict that erupted in 2023. In the months that followed, violence spread across Manipur’s districts, with Nagas and Kukis ransacking villages, laying ambushes and mutilating bodies. The clashes have claimed 65 lives, including three in Noney district on Saturday, taking the overall death toll from ethnic violence in Manipur in three years to at least 363. Thousands have been displaced. The events that unfolded that night in Litan village remain contested, with conflicting accounts of who started the fight and what followed. items.text: Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah is expected to visit India in late November and foreign secretary Vikram Misri is set to travel to Kathmandu next week as part of preparations for the Nepalese leader’s first bilateral foreign trip, persons aware of the matter said on Saturday. The rapper-turned-politician has shied away from foreign trips since he became PM in March and made his only multilateral foreign visit in September to New York to attend the UN General Assembly. Shah, who is known for his unconventional ways of functioning, is expected to visit India around November 22, the people said on condition of anonymity. India’s ambassador-designate to Nepal, senior career diplomat Sudhakar Dalela, is set to arrive in Kathmandu early next week, and this will be followed by Misri’s visit to Nepal on November 4 as part of preparations for Shah’s visit, the people said. Besides firming up the agenda for Shah’s visit, Misri is expected to review bilateral ties during meetings with senior Nepalese officials. items.headline: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
items.blurb: The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind.
items.text: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has frozen around half of the funds stolen in a "complex" hack, after $6.3bn (£4.7bn) was accessed in what is believed to be a record heist. The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider. Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit. The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds. America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI. items.headline: French billionaire Xavier Niel gets CCI nod for 16.2% Vodafone stake: What is the €5.1 billion deal?
items.blurb: The CCI has approved French billionaire Xavier Niel's €5.1 billion deal to acquire a 16.2% stake in Vodafone Group through his investment vehicle Vega SAS. The acquisition, from Emirates Telecommunications Group, will make Vega Vodafone's largest shareholder.
items.text: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) on Friday approved French billionaire Xavier Niel's proposal to acquire a 16.2% stake in UK-based telecom major Vodafone Group Plc, news agency PTI reported. The deal, valued at around €5.1 billion, involves the purchase of the stake by Vega SAS, Niel's family investment vehicle, from Emirates Telecommunications Group Co PJSC. Once completed, Vega SAS is expected to become Vodafone's single largest shareholder, as per the PTI report. Niel, the founder of French telecom company Iliad, is making the acquisition through Vega SAS, a wholly owned subsidiary of Maya SAS, a company incorporated under French law. In a post on X, the competition watchdog said it had approved the acquisition of 16.2% of Vodafone Group's issued share capital. Although Vega SAS has no direct business operations in India, the transaction required scrutiny from the Indian competition regulator because of Vodafone's presence in the domestic telecom market. Vodafone operates in India through its joint venture, Vodafone Idea Ltd. items.blurb: Running a clinic involves more than examining patients. Like any business, doctors also need to manage their schedules, patient records,…

items.text: Double Olympic medallist P.V. Sindhu, who finished runner-up at the French Open last week, continued her impressive run with a 21–13, 21–16 win over World No. 53 Anmol in a lopsided 32-minute semifinal. Anmol, 19, was playing in just her second Super 500 semifinal, having reached the last four at the Arctic Open last year. It was a similar story on Saturday as Sindhu’s attacking game, precise net play and wider repertoire of strokes ensured that Anmol could not put her illustrious compatriot under pressure. items.blurb: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded.
items.text: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded. Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI. In the months since, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have also disclosed incidents in which their agents have gone off track. And worryingly, in many cases the agents eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them. AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts. They must do more to ensure safety. That’s why EU regulators and US agencies are rightfully calling for agent developers and deployers to monitor agents in real time. items.text: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers’ machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont. Both Beaumont and the CTO and co-founder of security firm Phorian said that version 2.1.313 was distributed through Anthropic’s official account on Cursor. So far, neither Cursor nor Anthropic has explained how the attackers gained control of the account. “It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel,” Phorian CTO and co-founder Luke Roberts told Ars. “The malicious version 2.1.313 was posted to the official Anthropic account, effectively superseding 2.1.312. items.text: Across a business, any number of AI platforms, systems, and tools may be at work simultaneously—for example, AI-powered customer platforms, conversational assistants, and workflow and process automation tools. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond. But, when set to work, the outcomes and actions that emerge may be wrong, confused, or lacking a proper understanding of the business. Many organizations find themselves in this situation—and it could be one of key reasons they struggle to extract returns on their AI investments. An MIT Technology Review Insights poll finds that while every organization surveyed is using AI today to some degree, fewer than one in five (16%) are extracting transformative value from their deployments. The largest percentage of respondents (40%) say they are seeing moderate gains in specific tasks or teams, while 21% report meaningful gains, leaving 23% that are seeing minimal returns or none at all. items.headline: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
items.text: Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync. Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities. Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems. items.text: Google’s AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space: Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google’s Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this month . “Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit,” Google says. “Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027.” Sign in to see your notifications or create an account to join the conversation.

Anthropic is expected to receive a high “junk” rating from credit rating agencies following its initial public offering, according to a report from the Financial Times. The FT says the investment giant Blackstone, the anchor investor in a recent $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic’s chips, told investors in the deal that it expects the AI lab to receive a “high” junk rating after its IPO. Previously, the FT notes, Blackstone had said the opposite: that the Claude maker would receive an investment-grade rating (indicating low risk for lenders) before 2027 rolls around. Now Blackstone expects double B range rating, the top tier of speculative “junk” grade, according to the reporting. TechCrunch reached out to Anthropic and Blackstone but both declined to comment.
